subject: BeaconHealth cost sizing & concurrency checklist
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@beaconhealth.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: BeaconHealth cost sizing & concurrency checklist

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier. I wanted to capture our shared assumptions and the concrete items we agreed to confirm so we can size a clean cost projection and recommend a batching/concurrency configuration. Please review the bullets below and reply with any corrections.

Key takeaways from call:
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + patient Q&A microflows. Many short requests (avg ~220–350 tokens) coming from in-app interactions.
- Expected monthly token volume: your initial plan was ~1M–10M tokens/month; you mentioned a potential stretch to ~15M in peak months.
- Peak concurrent active requests: you said spikes could reach up to ~70–80 concurrent sessions but steady-state concurrency looks closer to 20–40.
- Request pattern: evenly distributed during business hours with a long tail overnight (we called this "continuous batching" scenario) — lots of small requests rather than large single prompts.
- Budget range (monthly): you gave a ballpark of $6k–$12k/month for inference (excluding integration/support).
- Target unit price: you indicated a target of roughly $75–$95 per 1M tokens (we discussed aiming near $85/1M).

Immediate asks / next steps (from Redwood):
1) Confirm the monthly token range you want us to model (pick a conservative and a stretch case).
2) Tell us the average request size you want us to assume for econ modeling (we have 220 and 350 as candidates).
3) Confirm whether streaming responses are required for the Q&A flows (this impacts batching and latency).
4) We'll send a first-pass cost model (attached) and a recommended batching/config brief for continuous small-request patterns.
5) If the numbers look good, schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (we'll invite infra + runtime) to lock parameters (batch window, buffer caps, preferred quantization).

Attachments: beacon_econ_model_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — first-pass costing; batching_config_recommendation.pdf (pdf) — short recommendation.

Proposed dates for deep-dive: Mon 3/22 or Tue 3/23 (your timezone).

If anything above is off, say so and we'll update the sheets.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@beaconhealth.ai>

Cc: BeaconHealth Solutions <sa@beaconhealth.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BeaconHealth cost sizing & concurrency checklist

Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sending the initial files. A few clarifications from our side:
- Monthly volume: planning case 5M tokens/month; stretch case 12–15M tokens/month (our pilot target is 5M).
- Avg request size: please model both 220 tokens (Q&A microflows) and 320 tokens (note summarization after pre-processing).
- Peak concurrency: our ops team said spikes have hit ~80 concurrent during rolling clinic launches; steady-state ~25.
- Streaming: required for the patient Q&A microflows — low-latency streaming improves UX.
- Budget: the $6k–$12k was the team-side budget we discussed; we'll push for the high end during procurement but need to see unit economics.
- Unit target: personally prefer $75/1M but leadership may accept up to $95/1M depending on latency SLAs and retention guarantees.

Two quick asks from BeaconHealth: (1) Can you show a hosted vs dedicated cost comparison in the econ model? (2) Call out expected RTT/cold-start latency impact when streaming is enabled.

I'll pencil in Mon 3/22 for the deep-dive — please send a calendar invite.

Best,
Emma Lawson
Head of Product Integrations
BeaconHealth
emma.lawson@beaconhealth.ai

Subject: Internal: BeaconHealth numbers + ask

Rishi / Monica —

Looping you in with BeaconHealth's clarified numbers (Emma replied, copied below). Key variance vs our first pass: planning 5M / stretch 12–15M tokens; avg sizes: 220 (Q&A) and 320 (summaries); streaming required for Q&A; peaks up to ~80 concurrency.

What I need from you:
- Rishi: please update the econ model for both hosting options (hosted API and dedicated reserved capacity) using these two volume scenarios. Call out unit $/1M tokens under continuous batching assumptions we would apply for short requests with streaming. Please include: per-1M token price, expected monthly bill for planning and stretch, and rough latency targets (p50/p95) for streaming enabled vs disabled.
- Monica: prep a short one-pager for procurement explaining trade-offs (cost vs SLA vs isolation) — include recommended fallback (e.g., hosted + reserved burst or dedicated pool).

Operational assumptions I think we should use for modeling (please confirm or adjust):
- Continuous batching window: 40–80ms (short requests aggregated into micro-batches to preserve latency).
- Buffer cap: 64 concurrent in-window requests (circuit-breaker above this sends request to the next pool or throttles).
- Default quantization plan: int8 for the dedicated option; mixed-int8/float16 for hosted if needed to guarantee p95 latency.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching is small here, but leverage short-term KV for repeated prompts (estimated 3–5% token reduction).

Timeline: Can you have an updated econ + latency slide by Fri EOD (3/19)? Emma asked for a hosted vs dedicated comparison ahead of her procurement sync next week.

Thanks — I can host the technical deep-dive on Mon 3/22 at 10am PT if that works for you both.

-Steph

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 01:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: BeaconHealth numbers + ask

Perfect — thanks for the summary. I'll run two detailed scenarios and return a short slide + numbers tomorrow morning (Fri 3/19):

Scenario A (planning): 5M tokens/month
Scenario B (stretch): 12–15M tokens/month

Initial modeling notes (high level before the slide):
- Continuous batching: using a 50ms batching window + buffer cap 64 produces the best tradeoff for sub-350-token requests. This assumes steady arrival rates; under bursty spikes we recommend autoscale to a dedicated burst pool.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: hosted looks competitive at ~5M tokens and if Beacon accepts slightly higher p95 latency for streaming; dedicated becomes >1.5x unit-efficiency at ~12M tokens but requires a 3–6 month commitment for reserved savings.
- Pricing: I'll produce $/1M-token bands around $70–$110 depending on config, quantization, and cache assumptions; target row will highlight a mid-point $82/1M for a mixed quant + caching config.
- Latency: with streaming enabled + continuous batching window 50ms we should see p50 ~55–75ms and p95 ~240–320ms for the Q&A paths (depending on model choice). We'll include model variants in the slide.

I'll attach the updated beacon_econ_model_v2.xlsx and a short batching recommendation PDF when done. If you want, I can also add a short table showing break-even token volume where dedicated becomes cheaper.

I'll join the Mon 3/22 10am PT deep-dive.

Rishi

Redwood Inference
